title: Annotatio V §.I open: Manducatio propria vs impropria — physical eating into mouth and stomach
pass_a_gloss: ANNOTATION V. On the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body. §. I. EATING, designating a certain action, is either Proper or Improper. PROPER is a Physical or natural action, consisting in the taking of some Corporal foodstuff, or foodstuff properly so called, into the body’s mouth, and the sending of the same down into the stomach. Whence for eating properly so called these Three things are required as essential: (1) Corporal Foodstuff, as Object of the action; (2) a Double Corporal Action about the object, of which the Prior is finished by taking / receiving the corporal foodstuff into the mouth; the Posterior by sending it down into the stomach. Each action is equally necessary for eating properly so called: for he is not said properly to eat, i.e. to eat physically, who only receives foodstuff into the mouth soon to emit the same from the mouth, but he only who also sends the foodstuff received into the mouth down through the throat into the stomach.
pass_b_english: Annotatio V opens on Oral Eating of Christ’s Body. §.I: Eating is Proper or Improper.
PROPER is physical: take corporal food into the mouth and send it down into the stomach — both reception and swallowing required; mouth-only then spit-out is not proper eating.
source_text: ANNOTATIO V. De Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali. §. I. MANDUCATIO, actionem quandam designans, vel Propria est, vel Impropria. PROPRIA est actio Physica, seu naturalis, consistens in assumptione esculenti alicujus Corporalis, seu propriè sic dicti, in os corporis, demissioneque ejusdem in stomachum. Unde ad propriè dictam Manducationem hæc Tria, tanquam essentialia, requiruntur (1) Esculentum Corporale, ceu Objectum actionis (2) Duplex Actio Corporalis circa objectum, quarum Prior esculenti corporalis assumptione, seu receptione in os; Posterior demissione ejus in stomachum absolvitur. Utraque actio ad Manducationem propriè sic dictam, æquè necessaria: neque enim ille propriè manducare, i. e. physicè edere dicitur, qui esculentum in os solummodò recipit, mox idem ex ore emissurus, sed is demum, qui receptum in os esculentum, etiam per guttur in stomachum demittit.
notes: Annotatio V §.I open: propria = mouth + stomach.
